about: Per-system driver rules. A rule applies when every key in its match is true for this machine. conf entries are written to /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/nvrm610.conf (the driver reads them at load); builtin rules live in the driver's code and are listed so reports show which ones this machine gets.

rules.why: The driver has hardware encoders for Turing (GTX 16 and RTX 20), Ampere and Blackwell, but none yet for Ada; on Ada apps use Apple's software encoder instead of failing. This rule once covered Turing and Ampere too and kept their encoders off after the driver gained them.
evidence: Discord 2026-10-07: RTX 3050 can decode but not encode (before the Ampere encoder)
Discord 2026-10-20: RTX 3080 Ti encodes H.264 and HEVC 8/8 once this rule's knobs are removed

rules.why: Turing needs the graphics engine's partner copy engine named when its copy object is made (driver 1.0.7).
evidence: GTX 1650 Mobile: VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN at the copy object

rules.why: On Turing the desktop starts only when command buffers and system memory are not cached by the GPU; an RTX 2060 SUPER boot-looped at login without these two knobs and loads to a Metal 3 desktop with them (driver 1.0.11, no boot-arg needed).
evidence: GitHub issue 5 RTX 2060 SUPER: CE0 runlist errors, login loop; fixed by these two knobs alone

rules.why: Tiled images are sized to the 64 KB range they are bound with, before Blackwell (driver 1.0.6/1.0.7).
evidence: RTX 3050: WindowServer abort on a resolution change

rules.why: Behind Thunderbolt or a PCIe switch the driver does not move the card's memory window (driver 1.0.6).
A card that starts with a small BAR1 is resized to at most 8 GB (driver 1.0.6).
evidence: RTX 3060 and RTX 5080 stopped at 16 GB
